fl: ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:24 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the coming together of 1:18 is the taking into his house, and she was already his wife before it." -- ANSWER: "The finding in 1:18 raised the intent to put her away (1:19). The angel's "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (1:20) answered that intent. The text sets the conception before any taking, which is what D1 says." -- MEETS -- "took unto him his wife"
cr: ENFORCER AGREE (right: MEETS): "The text sets the conception before any taking, which is what D1 says" takes up the taking of 1:24 and shows the fit for the answering case. (judge wrote MEETS; RECORD-ONLY TRIAL, ruling 428)

fl: ANSWER CHECK: Deuteronomy 22:24 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the law calls a betrothed damsel a wife, so the espousal is marriage." -- ANSWER: "A husband who knew himself the source would have no one to expose and nothing to put away. The text records the intent, and 1:20 then answers it with a source other than himself. The grounds of 1:19 are real, and the answer to them in 1:20 is the Holy Ghost." -- MEETS -- "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife"
cr: ENFORCER DISAGREE (right: MISSES): the answer never touches the pressed point that the law calls a betrothed damsel a wife, speaking only of "A husband who knew himself the source would have no one to expose." (judge wrote MEETS; RECORD-ONLY TRIAL, ruling 428)

fl: ANSWER CHECK: Genesis 4:1 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the canon's stated means of begetting is the husband knowing his wife." -- ANSWER: "Genesis gives the ordinary means: the knowing, then the conception. Luke 1:34 states her own condition, and 1:35 states what shall come upon her. The pattern shows what the ordinary means is. It is not the means stated in Luke 1:35." -- MEETS -- "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"
cr: ENFORCER AGREE (right: MEETS): "The pattern shows what the ordinary means is. It is not the means stated in Luke 1:35" acknowledges the stated means and distinguishes Luke's. (judge wrote MEETS; RECORD-ONLY TRIAL, ruling 428)

fl: ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:25 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the abstaining is bounded from the taking to the birth." -- ANSWER: "The challenger places the husband's knowing inside the espousal, between 1:18 and 1:24. Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the coming together. Luke 2:5 still calls her "espoused" while she is great with child. No row has the knowing before the finding, so the link stands." -- MEETS -- "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"
cr: ENFORCER AGREE (right: MEETS): "Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the coming together" places the conception outside the span the press bounds. (judge wrote MEETS; RECORD-ONLY TRIAL, ruling 428)

fl: ANSWER CHECK: John 1:13 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "born of God is a sonship given to men who have fathers in the flesh." -- ANSWER: "The "of God" in 1:13 is set against "the will of man". It cannot be turned into "of God, plus man's begetting". Matthew 1:20 has the same preposition ek ("out of") with the Holy Ghost as source, and the verse's own contrast excludes the will of man." -- MEETS -- "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
cr: ENFORCER AGREE (right: MEETS): "the verse's own contrast excludes the will of man" meets the claim that born-of-God sonship sits alongside human begetting. (judge wrote MEETS; RECORD-ONLY TRIAL, ruling 428)
